• Swollen ankles and fluid retention
• Fatigue and reduced exercise endurance
• Muscle cramps, twitching, and tremors
• Irregular heart rhythms
• Constipation
• Difficulty sleeping

Potassium also plays an important role in stomach acid balance, protein digestion, and calcium regulation. Getting enough potassium helps your muscles, nerves, and digestive system function properly while supporting healthy blood pressure and circulation.

videos.title: Google Genie 4 Is INSANE: AI Can Now Create Worlds You Can Play In!
videos.summary_source_text:
Google Genie 4 Is INSANE: AI Can Now Create Worlds You Can Play In! Google DeepMind just unveiled Genie 4, its most realistic AI world model yet. It generates photorealistic, interactive worlds with real-time audio, changing weather, and AI-controlled characters. But there's a catch: these worlds only stay consistent for about TWO MINUTES.

Announced on October 27, Genie 4 goes far beyond traditional AI video generation. Instead of producing a fixed video, Google's world model lets you step inside an AI-generated environment, explore it using WASD controls, interact with objects, and modify the scene while it's running.

There's no traditional game engine underneath. Every frame is synthesized by AI, with Google's Gemini Omni providing the visual foundation.

And the demonstrations are impressive.

Google showcased a dragon flying at approximately 140 km/h, a jazz saxophonist performing on a floating platform, a hot-air balloon over Antarctica, a crowded 1980s Japanese train station, and an entire stained-glass world.

Even more interesting are the physics demonstrations: flowing satin fabric reacting to wind and a spinning maple seed falling through the air.

But these carefully selected demos raise an important question: How well does Genie 4 handle unpredictable interactions outside Google's controlled examples?

One of Genie 4's biggest upgrades is native audio generation.

Unlike Genie 3, which generated silent worlds, Genie 4 produces environmental sounds, music, and character dialogue alongside its visuals. The dragon demo includes wind and wingbeats, the saxophone performance features synchronized jazz, and characters can even converse in different languages.

However, DeepMind reportedly acknowledges that audio accuracy remains a work in progress.

Then there's the Gemini integration.

Google demonstrated a system where Gemini acts as a director, breaking complex goals into individual instructions, sending them to Genie 4, reviewing the generated results, and adjusting its next actions.

In one example, Gemini guides a simulated Apptronik Apollo humanoid robot through a game of checkers.

This could eventually matter for AI agents, robotics training, and artificial general intelligence (AGI). But it's important to distinguish a simulated robot demonstration from proven real-world robotic capabilities.

The biggest limitation is still world consistency.

After approximately two minutes, Genie 4 can begin losing object permanence. Textures drift, characters may change appearance, and objects don't always remain where they should.

There's also no dedicated physics engine. Genie 4 learns physical behavior from video rather than calculating it through traditional simulations.

And generating readable text inside these worlds remains a challenge.

Google also hasn't released a Genie 4 research paper or model card, and independent researchers haven't yet verified its performance.

So how does it compare with the competition?

Runway's GWM Worlds 2 offers continuous generation at 720p and 24 FPS with 48 kHz audio. Decart's Oasis 3 focuses on robotics applications, while World Labs' Marble creates persistent 3D environments that can be revisited.

Genie 4's potential advantage lies in its claimed photorealism, interactive audio, and integration with Gemini's reasoning capabilities. But without independent head-to-head benchmarks, there's no confirmed winner.

Availability is another limitation.

Genie 4 is currently a restricted research preview, with Google planning access through Project Genie for Google AI Ultra subscribers and selected developers through the Gemini API and Google AI Studio.

In this video, we examine what Google actually demonstrated, how Genie 4 compares with Genie 1, Genie 2, and Genie 3, what its technical limitations reveal, and whether AI-generated interactive worlds could eventually transform gaming, filmmaking, robotics, and AGI research.

The bigger question isn't whether Genie 4 can generate an impressive world for two minutes.

It's whether Google can make that world persistent, reliable, and physically consistent enough to become genuinely useful.

Is Genie 4 the future of interactive AI, or are we still watching carefully curated technology demos?

Share your thoughts in the comments, and subscribe to BitBiased for independent analysis of AI breakthroughs, emerging technology, and the competition shaping the future.

videos.title: China Just Released a 2.8 TRILLION Parameter AI — Beats GPT-6 Astra!
videos.summary_source_text:
China Just Released a 2.8 TRILLION Parameter AI — Beats GPT-6 Astra! Moonshot AI's Kimi K3.1 Pro just scored 67% on Terminal-Bench 4.0 in independent testing, beating Claude Sonnet 5.5 and recording the highest score Artificial Analysis had measured at publication. Its predecessor, Kimi K3, managed just 13%. That's a massive 54-point improvement without building an entirely new foundation model.

But here's the twist: despite that record-breaking result, Kimi K3.1 Pro ranks only fourth overall on Artificial Analysis's Intelligence Index, behind Claude Opus 5.5 and other frontier models.

So is China's latest AI model genuinely challenging OpenAI and Anthropic, or are the headlines missing something important?

Moonshot AI launched Kimi K3.1 Pro on October 24, 2026, with major improvements in autonomous coding, agentic workflows, long-context reasoning, and tool use. Unlike previous releases focused on scaling model size, K3.1 builds on Kimi K3's existing mixture-of-experts architecture, featuring approximately 2.8 trillion total parameters and 104 billion active parameters.

Independent benchmarks reveal a complicated picture.

Artificial Analysis measured Kimi K3.1 Pro at 67% on Terminal-Bench 4.0, ahead of Claude Sonnet 5.5's 64%. AutomationBench performance jumped from 58% to 73%, while its Intelligence Index increased from 44 to 55.

However, Claude Opus 5.5 still leads overall with an Intelligence Index of 58. Kimi also trails leading competitors in web development and scientific agent tasks.

And Moonshot's own benchmark comparisons require careful interpretation. Different evaluation harnesses, scoring methods, and testing configurations make some headline comparisons less definitive than they appear.

Then there are Kimi's ambitious demonstrations.

Moonshot showcased an AI agent developing a human walking simulator involving 296 skeletal components and 402 muscle components. After 167 missions and 420 reviews, the company says its system achieved 11.2 seconds of alternating stride.

Kimi K3.1 Pro also generates 3D environments using Blender, CAD tools, Three.js, Unity, Unreal Engine, and Godot.

But this isn't a native 3D foundation model. Kimi creates 3D content primarily by writing and executing code through existing software tools. And several impressive demonstrations still lack independent reproduction.

The cybersecurity story is even more interesting.

Moonshot disclosed that it deliberately reduced Kimi K3.1 Pro's vulnerability-exploitation capabilities during training.

On its internal xdev-bench-hard benchmark, an unfiltered checkpoint scored 90.5%, while the released model scored 81.0%. The previous Kimi K3 scored just 33.3%.

That means Moonshot reportedly weakened the model's offensive cybersecurity abilities without eliminating them. These results remain independently unverified.

This raises difficult questions about AI safety, open-weight releases, and whether dangerous capabilities can be selectively reduced without affecting legitimate programming skills.

And speaking of open weights, Moonshot has promised to release Kimi K3.1 Pro's weights by November 4, 2026.

If delivered, Artificial Analysis projects it could become the highest-scoring open-weight model on its Intelligence Index, dramatically narrowing the gap with proprietary AI systems.

But until the weights arrive, that remains a promise rather than a completed release.

Pricing adds another dimension.

Kimi K3.1 Pro costs approximately $2 per million input tokens and $10 per million output tokens at tracked international rates.

That's roughly 80% cheaper than GPT-6 Astra and half the price of Claude Opus 5.5.

However, DeepSeek V4.1 Flash remains significantly cheaper, and Moonshot's faster Kimi Highspeed option comes at approximately double the cost.

There are also practical concerns about inference speed, reasoning-token consumption, hardware requirements, API reliability, and the rate limits users encountered following launch.

So where does Kimi K3.1 Pro actually stand against GPT-6 Astra, Claude Opus 5.5, Gemini 4 Argon, and DeepSeek?

We examine the independent benchmarks, Moonshot's technical claims, the 3D demonstrations, cybersecurity filtering, open-weight promises, and the real cost of running this model.

Because the biggest story might not be that Kimi beat a frontier model on one benchmark.

It might be what Moonshot achieved without building a bigger foundation model.

We test all the big names (TaylorMade, Callaway, Ping, Titleist, Mizuno, Cobra and more) plus the direct-to-consumer brands you’re starting to hear about. New vs old, budget vs premium, “forgiving” vs “players” – we put them head-to-head so you can see what actually performs.

Our testing is built around launch monitor data (GCQuad) and real-world shots, but we always explain the numbers in normal-golfer language. No fluff, no hidden agendas – just whether a club will help your game or not.

buying your first proper set,
a mid-handicapper looking for more forgiveness, or
a low-handicap player chasing that perfect combo of feel and distance,

To cut through the hype.
To give golfers the truth.

videos.title: 27.10.26 - RIFT Presentation
videos.summary_source_text:
27.10.26 - RIFT Presentation RIFT is a modern, non-custodial trading and financial technology ecosystem designed to bring together market access, education, intelligent execution, portfolio participation and professional trading infrastructure in one connected environment.

Built for both newcomers and experienced market participants, RIFT provides a structured journey from learning and practice through to increasingly sophisticated forms of market participation.

ONE ECOSYSTEM. MULTIPLE WAYS TO PARTICIPATE.

RIFT gives users access to a range of trading and financial tools, including:

• Demo Trading — Practice market participation using virtual capital while learning how markets, execution and platform functionality work.

• Spot Trading — Participate directly in spot markets while developing an understanding of market behaviour, patience and risk management.

• Futures Trading — Access leveraged markets with tools and functionality designed for more advanced trading strategies and risk management.

• Smart Money — Explore structured portfolio participation through features including mirror wallets and trading books, allowing users to move beyond focusing only on individual trades.

• Auto Trading Engine — Access structured automated execution through different environments designed to support systematic and repeatable participation.

• Prediction Markets — Participate in an emerging category of market infrastructure where users can trade contracts based on the probability of future events and outcomes.

• Prop Trading Infrastructure — Learn about and participate in the evolving world of proprietary trading, funded accounts, capital allocation, performance evaluation and professional risk management.

INTELLIGENT FINANCIAL INFRASTRUCTURE

RIFT is designed around the idea that the future of finance will combine human decision-making with intelligent technology.

Modern financial markets generate enormous amounts of information. Algorithms and AI systems can process data, identify patterns, monitor markets and support execution at a speed that is impossible for an individual human to replicate.

RIFT explores how these technologies can work alongside human judgement to create more structured and intelligent financial participation.

The objective is not simply to automate everything.

It is to combine people, data, technology, risk management and intelligent execution within a connected financial ecosystem.

EDUCATION AT THE CORE

RIFT places strong emphasis on education and developing a deeper understanding of financial markets.

Through the RIFT Before You Quit educational series, training sessions and community learning, participants explore subjects including:

• Trading psychology
• Risk management
• Capital preservation
• Portfolio construction
• Capital allocation
• Market structure
• Smart money concepts
• Futures and leverage
• Prediction markets
• Proprietary trading
• Behavioural finance
• Artificial intelligence
• Algorithmic execution
• Financial infrastructure
• Professional trading principles

The objective is to help participants understand not only how to participate in markets, but also why disciplined decision-making matters.

A STRUCTURED LEARNING JOURNEY

RIFT is designed to provide a progression from education and practice toward more advanced market participation:

Learn → Demo → Spot → Futures → Smart Money → Automated Execution → Professional Trading

Each stage introduces different concepts, technologies and levels of responsibility.

Rather than focusing solely on individual trades or short-term results, RIFT encourages participants to develop a broader understanding of risk, process, discipline and capital management.

NON-CUSTODIAL INFRASTRUCTURE

RIFT follows a non-custodial approach designed to give users greater control over their own funds and reduce the need to place assets into a centralized company-controlled account.

This reflects a broader movement within digital finance toward greater transparency, user control and blockchain-based infrastructure.

ACCESS FROM ANY DEVICE

RIFT is available through the web as well as its broader platform environment, making it accessible across modern computers, smartphones and other devices.

Its lightweight infrastructure is designed to make participation practical even for users with older devices, helping remove unnecessary technology barriers to accessing modern financial tools.

THE FUTURE OF FINANCIAL PARTICIPATION

Financial markets are changing rapidly.

Trading is becoming increasingly automated. Artificial intelligence is transforming data analysis. Prediction markets are creating new forms of information-based participation. Proprietary trading is expanding access to structured capital allocation models. Blockchain infrastructure is changing how digital assets can be held and transferred.

RIFT brings these developments together within one evolving ecosystem.

videos.summary_source_text:
Hindi - 27.10.26 - RIFT Presentation RIFT is a modern, non-custodial trading and financial technology ecosystem designed to bring together market access, education, intelligent execution, portfolio participation and professional trading infrastructure in one connected environment.

Built for both newcomers and experienced market participants, RIFT provides a structured journey from learning and practice through to increasingly sophisticated forms of market participation.

ONE ECOSYSTEM. MULTIPLE WAYS TO PARTICIPATE.

RIFT gives users access to a range of trading and financial tools, including:

• Demo Trading — Practice market participation using virtual capital while learning how markets, execution and platform functionality work.

• Spot Trading — Participate directly in spot markets while developing an understanding of market behaviour, patience and risk management.

• Futures Trading — Access leveraged markets with tools and functionality designed for more advanced trading strategies and risk management.

• Smart Money — Explore structured portfolio participation through features including mirror wallets and trading books, allowing users to move beyond focusing only on individual trades.

• Auto Trading Engine — Access structured automated execution through different environments designed to support systematic and repeatable participation.

• Prediction Markets — Participate in an emerging category of market infrastructure where users can trade contracts based on the probability of future events and outcomes.

• Prop Trading Infrastructure — Learn about and participate in the evolving world of proprietary trading, funded accounts, capital allocation, performance evaluation and professional risk management.

INTELLIGENT FINANCIAL INFRASTRUCTURE

RIFT is designed around the idea that the future of finance will combine human decision-making with intelligent technology.

Modern financial markets generate enormous amounts of information. Algorithms and AI systems can process data, identify patterns, monitor markets and support execution at a speed that is impossible for an individual human to replicate.

RIFT explores how these technologies can work alongside human judgement to create more structured and intelligent financial participation.

The objective is not simply to automate everything.

It is to combine people, data, technology, risk management and intelligent execution within a connected financial ecosystem.

EDUCATION AT THE CORE

RIFT places strong emphasis on education and developing a deeper understanding of financial markets.

Through the RIFT Before You Quit educational series, training sessions and community learning, participants explore subjects including:

• Trading psychology
• Risk management
• Capital preservation
• Portfolio construction
• Capital allocation
• Market structure
• Smart money concepts
• Futures and leverage
• Prediction markets
• Proprietary trading
• Behavioural finance
• Artificial intelligence
• Algorithmic execution
• Financial infrastructure
• Professional trading principles

The objective is to help participants understand not only how to participate in markets, but also why disciplined decision-making matters.

A STRUCTURED LEARNING JOURNEY

RIFT is designed to provide a progression from education and practice toward more advanced market participation:

Learn → Demo → Spot → Futures → Smart Money → Automated Execution → Professional Trading

Each stage introduces different concepts, technologies and levels of responsibility.

Rather than focusing solely on individual trades or short-term results, RIFT encourages participants to develop a broader understanding of risk, process, discipline and capital management.

NON-CUSTODIAL INFRASTRUCTURE

RIFT follows a non-custodial approach designed to give users greater control over their own funds and reduce the need to place assets into a centralized company-controlled account.

This reflects a broader movement within digital finance toward greater transparency, user control and blockchain-based infrastructure.

ACCESS FROM ANY DEVICE

RIFT is available through the web as well as its broader platform environment, making it accessible across modern computers, smartphones and other devices.

Its lightweight infrastructure is designed to make participation practical even for users with older devices, helping remove unnecessary technology barriers to accessing modern financial tools.

THE FUTURE OF FINANCIAL PARTICIPATION

Financial markets are changing rapidly.

Trading is becoming increasingly automated. Artificial intelligence is transforming data analysis. Prediction markets are creating new forms of information-based participation. Proprietary trading is expanding access to structured capital allocation models. Blockchain infrastructure is changing how digital assets can be held and transferred.

RIFT brings these developments together within one evolving ecosystem.

videos.title: Paul Maurice, Panthers Postgame: Florida Ends Road Trip in Style, Ground Winnipeg Jets
videos.summary_source_text:
Paul Maurice, Panthers Postgame: Florida Ends Road Trip in Style, Ground Winnipeg Jets Florida Panthers coach Paul Maurice speaks to the media in Winnipeg after his team beat the host Jets 5-1 on Tuesday, Oct. 27, 2026.

Florida ends this road trip with two straight wins after losing in Ottawa and Pittsburgh. 

The Panthers took a 3-0 lead into the second off a pair of power-play goals from Carter Verhaeghe and one from Niko Mikkola. 

Florida had five players with multi-point games including Matthew Tkachuk (four assists), Seth Jones (three assists), and Brady Tkachuk (goal, two assists). 

Akira Schmid made 24 saves for his second straight win and fourth in the past five. 

Florida heads home and will play host to this same Jets team in Sunrise on Friday night.

videos.title: Akira Schmid Stays Hot, Backstops Florida Panthers to Win at Winnipeg Jets
videos.summary_source_text:
Akira Schmid Stays Hot, Backstops Florida Panthers to Win at Winnipeg Jets Florida Panthers goalie Akira Schmid speaks to the media in Winnipeg after his team beat the host Jets 5-1 on Tuesday, Oct. 27, 2026.

Florida ends this road trip with two straight wins after losing in Ottawa and Pittsburgh. 

The Panthers took a 3-0 lead into the second off a pair of power-play goals from Carter Verhaeghe and one from Niko Mikkola. 

Florida had five players with multi-point games including Matthew Tkachuk (four assists), Seth Jones (three assists), and Brady Tkachuk (goal, two assists). 

Akira Schmid made 24 saves for his second straight win and fourth in the past five. 

Florida heads home and will play host to this same Jets team in Sunrise on Friday night.

videos.summary_source_text:
The Amazing Benefits of Eating Eggs Eggs are much more than just a source of protein. A single egg contains over 850 different proteins, along with important nutrients that support brain health, memory, and immune function.

Watch the FULL video here: ▶️https://youtu.be/Oyboz_CThiE

🌟 Take the 2-minute Health Lever Quiz: https://drbrg.co/47CdH0k

Just so you know, my full line of high-quality supplements is available on Amazon — search Dr. Berg Supplements.   

Some of the beneficial compounds found in eggs include:
• Lysozyme, a protein with natural antibacterial properties
• IgY antibodies, studied for their effects on H. pylori
• Cystatin, a protein studied for memory improvements in Alzheimer’s animal models
• Choline, essential for producing acetylcholine, a neurotransmitter involved in brain function and memory

Just two eggs provide approximately 300 mg of choline. Eggs also contain lutein, high-quality protein, and important B vitamins, including B1, B2, B6, and B12, making them one of the most nutrient-dense foods for brain health.

She Had Everything for a Great Golf Swing… Except This ⛳️ Take Your FREE Game Assessment → https://meandmygolf.com/game-plan/?utm_source=YouTube&utm_medium=Description&utm_campaign=27.10.26

📱 Download the Swing Coach App (2-Week Free Trial) → https://go.meandmygolf.com/swingcoach/yt/?utm_source=YouTube&utm_medium=Description&utm_campaign=27.10.26

Brittany had only been playing golf for around 12 months. Her golf swing looked great, but she was struggling to strike her irons consistently. In this live lesson, we worked through the issues that were making solid ball-then-turf contact so difficult.

First, we helped Brittany understand how to get the club swinging closer to the correct plane. This gave her a clearer picture of what an on-plane golf swing should look and feel like, as well as something she could continue working on after the lesson.

The biggest issue, however, was how she used her lower body. Brittany wasn’t creating enough stability or coil into her trail leg during the backswing. This made it difficult for her to engage the lower body, move forward through the shot and consistently strike the golf ball before the turf.

In this lesson, you’ll learn how to:
- Get the golf club moving closer to the correct swing plane
- Create a better backswing pivot without swaying
- Stabilise the trail leg and create a more powerful coil
- Use the lower body in a more athletic way
- Improve ball-then-turf contact with your irons

If your golf swing looks good but your ball striking remains inconsistent, this lesson could help you identify what’s missing.

videos.title: OpenAI’s GPT 6.1 Terra Is Insane — 10x Cheaper and 3x Faster!
videos.summary_source_text:
OpenAI’s GPT 6.1 Terra Is Insane — 10x Cheaper and 3x Faster! OpenAI's new GPT-6.1 Terra costs 90% less than GPT-6 Astra, completes certain AI agent tasks more than 3 times faster, and more than doubles its predecessor's Terminal-Bench score. But independent testing reveals a major catch: at maximum reasoning, Terra can take over a minute just to produce its first output.

So is GPT-6.1 Terra a genuine AI breakthrough, or has OpenAI simply made powerful AI agents dramatically cheaper?

The story actually started before OpenAI's October 26 announcement. Developers discovered references to GPT-6.1 Terra inside Microsoft's Entity Framework Core and GitHub Copilot testing code. These leaks suggested OpenAI was preparing a new model capable of handling complex reasoning, code reviews, and autonomous agent workflows.

Now that Terra is official, the numbers deserve a closer look.

GPT-6.1 Terra features a massive 1.05-million-token context window, up to 128,000 output tokens, six reasoning settings, and native support for computer-use workflows through external tools. It can interpret screenshots, decide where to click, navigate applications, enter text, and interact with software.

But there's an important distinction: Terra doesn't directly control your computer. It generates actions that an external driver executes, and developers remain responsible for permissions, approvals, and verifying results.

The benchmark results are equally interesting.

On Terminal-Bench 4.0, GPT-6.1 Terra reportedly jumped from 21.5% to 50.3%. OpenAI's internal factual-error testing also showed error rates falling from 53.6% on the previous model at low effort to 16.7%, with the new model reaching 4.3% at maximum reasoning.

On Agents' Last Exam, OpenAI claims Terra performs roughly on par with Astra at medium reasoning effort while costing significantly less.

But independent results from Artificial Analysis tell a more nuanced story.

Terra scores 48 on the Artificial Analysis Intelligence Index, approximately four points behind GPT-6.1 Sol. Its Coding Agent Index score also trails Sol, 48 versus 54.

And while OpenAI advertises more than 3x faster task completion at maximum reasoning, Artificial Analysis measured approximately 78 seconds before the first output at that setting.

Then there's pricing.

GPT-6.1 Terra costs:
• $1 per million input tokens
• $5 per million output tokens
• $0.05 per million cached input tokens
• $0.50 input / $2.50 output with Batch or Flex

Compare that with GPT-6 Astra at $10/$50 and GPT-6.1 Sol at $2/$10.

Terra is 90% cheaper than Astra and 50% cheaper than Sol at standard rates.

However, screenshots, tool calls, hosted environments, retries, and human supervision can substantially increase the real cost of autonomous workflows. Pricing also changes when input exceeds 272,000 tokens.

We also examine how Terra compares with Anthropic's Claude Opus 5.5 and Google's Gemini 4 Argon.

OpenAI claims major cost-efficiency advantages against Claude on selected benchmarks, but independent, same-harness computer-use comparisons remain limited. Gemini also supports native audio and video capabilities that Terra lacks.

And security remains a serious concern.

OpenAI's safety evaluation covered 48,690 simulated tasks and recorded 22 severe flags. While that rate was relatively low, Terra showed weaker results in some lower-severity categories involving uncertainty, restrictions, and destructive actions.

Prompt injection, unauthorized actions, and human approval requirements haven't disappeared simply because the model is cheaper.

So what does GPT-6.1 Terra actually represent?

A major intelligence breakthrough? A more efficient GPT-6 model? Or a turning point in the economics of AI automation?

We break down the leaked evidence, OpenAI's benchmark claims, independent testing, pricing, computer-use architecture, security limitations, and the competitive implications for Claude and Gemini.

Watch before deciding whether Terra belongs in your next AI agent workflow.

Would you trust GPT-6.1 Terra to operate your computer autonomously? Let us know in the comments.

Subscribe to BitBiased for detailed AI model analysis, independent benchmark breakdowns, cybersecurity research, and emerging technology coverage.

A student came to Eric Cogorno struggling with weak right shots and poor contact — a pattern that had been holding him back for years — and made huge gains in 15 to 20 minutes from one micro move. The fix is the trail elbow pit pointing away from the body while the elbow works forward, combined with independent forearm rotation to square the club face at impact. Watch how Adam Scott and Tommy Fleetwood keep the elbow pit away throughout the entire downswing while forearm rotation delivers a square club face — and how the plate drill and ping pong paddle drill give any golfer the same feel immediately. These golf tips for beginners and improving golfers produce better golf swing consistency, solid contact, and a fix for the weak right miss that most golfers struggle with for years. If you leave this video without trying the plate drill, you’re leaving golf swing consistency and solid contact on the table.

• Why the trail elbow pit must point away from the body as the elbow works forward — and what happens when it rotates toward the target instead

• How Tommy Fleetwood uses the same elbow pit away position regardless of grip strength — and why every golfer needs some version of this move

• The ping pong paddle drill for feeling correct forearm rotation with the shoulder staying down through impact
• How to use ball flight as feedback — right miss means more rotation, left miss means less — for better golf swing consistency

videos.summary_source_text:
NEW SQ9 is the BIGGEST Audi EVER! Is the new Audi Q9 more luxurious than an A8?! 

Get 20% off CarVertical using code Carwow: https://www.carvertical.com/carwow

Mat’s flown over to Utah to get his hands on the Audi SQ9! 

It’s the first generation of the Audi Q9 & SQ9, and it sits right at the top of the Audi range. What’s more, it’s also the largest Audi ever produced! 

So with that in mind, should you choose it over class-leading 7-seaters like the BMW X7 and Mercedes GLS? Let’s take a closer look, starting with the design… 

From the outside, there’s no denying the all-new Q9 is a super large & imposing beast. Up front, there are similarities between the entry-level Q9 and this SQ9, although the latter has a more aggressive look to it, thanks to a different bumper and grille design. The large grille is flanked on either side by Audi’s class-leading DRLs, and the main headlights sit in a separate unit on the front end. Around the side, the SQ9 is given more definition thanks to chrome surrounds on the windows, chrome roof rails and creases along the doors. At the back, Audi has fitted the SQ9 with 100% real quad tailpipes, as well as wraparound OLED taillights!

On the inside, the SQ9 looks largely similar to all other recent Audis - but that’s no bad thing! The dashboard comes absolutely covered in screens, with the wraparound digital dial and infotainment screen, coupled with a passenger screen. There are little to no physical buttons, so everything is controlled through the screen. The materials are nice throughout the entire cabin, and the seats are large and comfortable. 

In the back, the SQ9 is available in a 6- or 7-seat configuration. The car we have here has the six seats, and the captain’s chairs are large, comfortable, and come with a high amount of movement. Simply put, the SQ9 is cavernous for passengers in the back! 

The Q9 series is available with a choice of either a V6 petrol or diesel, and a plug-in hybrid will also be available. However, in the range-topping SQ9 you’ll find a 4-litre twin-turbo V8 under the bonnet, and this delivers a huge 600hp and 800Nm of torque! 

As for price, the Q9 range starts from £103,900, rising to around £130,000 for this SQ9. But does it offer enough to sway you away from BMW or Mercedes? Let us know which you’d choose in the comments!

videos.title: 26.10.26 - Ep.26 (Part 2) - Execution, Market Makers & The True Cost of Liquidity
videos.summary_source_text:
26.10.26 - Ep.26 (Part 2) - Execution, Market Makers & The True Cost of Liquidity The price you see on a chart is not necessarily the price you receive. In Episode 26 Part 2, we explore execution, the hidden costs of trading, and the role market makers play in connecting buyers and sellers.

We also begin the transition from market understanding to practical prop-trading preparation: execute with awareness, measure risk, and review each decision.

THE LAST PRICE IS NOT YOUR PRICE

Charts show past transactions. Your order interacts with the market now, and its fill depends on the current bid and ask, depth, order queue, volatility, trade size, latency and competing orders.

Large orders may fill across several price levels. Even correct analysis can lose its edge through poor execution: being right about direction is not the same as trading well.

EXECUTION IS PART OF RISK MANAGEMENT

Risk begins with the order. Spreads, slippage, partial fills, market impact and limited exit liquidity can all change a trade's outcome.

The full cost of execution may include:
• Explicit trading fees
• The bid-ask spread
• Slippage
• Market impact
• Opportunity cost when an order never fills

For example, if you intend to deploy $100,000 and execution works against you by 20 basis points (0.20%), that difference equals $200. At 50 basis points, it equals $500. Repeated across trades, these costs matter.

PROP-TRADING READINESS: STAGE ONE

Professional trading means reviewing execution, not just profit and loss. Stage One is execution awareness: record how well you followed your process.

For every practice trade, record:
• Decision price
• Best bid and best ask
• Bid-ask spread
• Order type
• Intended entry and actual fill
• Slippage and position size
• Market conditions and exit type
• Execution notes

Use screenshots or screen recordings to review each order. Complete a daily execution sheet consistently. Ask: “Did I execute the plan correctly?” A winning trade can be poorly executed, while a losing trade can still reflect a disciplined process.

You do not need to trade faster, use more leverage or add ten new indicators. Observe carefully and understand the chain from decision, to order, to fill, to position, to exit. While practising, keep leverage low and focus on consistency rather than chasing profits.

Before every practice trade, ask:
• What size am I asking the market to fill, and at what price?
• What spread am I paying?
• How much liquidity is available?
• Which order type am I using?
• What happens if liquidity disappears before I exit?

Reviewing your records can help assess consistency and strategy performance. This is preparation for prop trading, not a promise of passing a challenge or making profits.

WHO PROVIDES LIQUIDITY?

Market makers stand between buyers and sellers by quoting prices at which they are willing to buy and sell. They help match buyers and sellers when natural counterparties are not immediately available.

For example, a market maker might quote a bid of $99.98 and an ask of $100.02. The difference is the spread. But market making is not simply buying low, selling high and collecting easy money. When a market maker buys an asset, it holds inventory and remains exposed to price movements until it can sell or hedge that position.

If a market maker buys 10,000 shares at $99.98 and the price falls to $99.50, the $0.48 move represents a $4,800 decline in the value of that inventory. Spread revenue is only one part of the economics; inventory risk, hedging, funding and fees also matter.

ADVERSE SELECTION & WIDENING SPREADS

Adverse selection is the risk of trading with someone whose information or reaction is better or faster. When prices rapidly re-adjust, a quote can become stale and expose the market maker to an unfavourable move.

This helps explain why spreads can widen during uncertainty. Before major economic news, volatility and hedging costs can rise. Market makers may respond with a lower bid and higher ask to compensate for added risk.

Liquidity is not fixed. It can become more expensive precisely when market participants most urgently need to trade.

THE PROFESSIONAL SHIFT

Episode 25 explored how capital moves. Episode 26 asks how the market absorbs that movement through liquidity, order books, spreads, execution and the participants willing to take the other side of a trade.

Questions evolve from “What is the price?” to “How much liquidity is available around that price?” From “I pressed Buy at $100” to “Where did my order actually fill?” And from “Was I right about direction?” to “Was my execution efficient, and did I follow my process?”

Next, we continue with market-maker inventory and how liquidity providers manage their exposure.

videos.title: Hindi - 26.10.26 - RIFT Presentation
videos.summary_source_text:
Hindi - 26.10.26 - RIFT Presentation RIFT is a modern, non-custodial trading and financial technology ecosystem designed to bring together market access, education, intelligent execution, portfolio participation and professional trading infrastructure in one connected environment.

Built for both newcomers and experienced market participants, RIFT provides a structured journey from learning and practice through to increasingly sophisticated forms of market participation.

ONE ECOSYSTEM. MULTIPLE WAYS TO PARTICIPATE.

RIFT gives users access to a range of trading and financial tools, including:

• Demo Trading — Practice market participation using virtual capital while learning how markets, execution and platform functionality work.

• Spot Trading — Participate directly in spot markets while developing an understanding of market behaviour, patience and risk management.

• Futures Trading — Access leveraged markets with tools and functionality designed for more advanced trading strategies and risk management.

• Smart Money — Explore structured portfolio participation through features including mirror wallets and trading books, allowing users to move beyond focusing only on individual trades.

• Auto Trading Engine — Access structured automated execution through different environments designed to support systematic and repeatable participation.

• Prediction Markets — Participate in an emerging category of market infrastructure where users can trade contracts based on the probability of future events and outcomes.

• Prop Trading Infrastructure — Learn about and participate in the evolving world of proprietary trading, funded accounts, capital allocation, performance evaluation and professional risk management.

INTELLIGENT FINANCIAL INFRASTRUCTURE

RIFT is designed around the idea that the future of finance will combine human decision-making with intelligent technology.

Modern financial markets generate enormous amounts of information. Algorithms and AI systems can process data, identify patterns, monitor markets and support execution at a speed that is impossible for an individual human to replicate.

RIFT explores how these technologies can work alongside human judgement to create more structured and intelligent financial participation.

The objective is not simply to automate everything.

It is to combine people, data, technology, risk management and intelligent execution within a connected financial ecosystem.

EDUCATION AT THE CORE

RIFT places strong emphasis on education and developing a deeper understanding of financial markets.

Through the RIFT Before You Quit educational series, training sessions and community learning, participants explore subjects including:

• Trading psychology
• Risk management
• Capital preservation
• Portfolio construction
• Capital allocation
• Market structure
• Smart money concepts
• Futures and leverage
• Prediction markets
• Proprietary trading
• Behavioural finance
• Artificial intelligence
• Algorithmic execution
• Financial infrastructure
• Professional trading principles

The objective is to help participants understand not only how to participate in markets, but also why disciplined decision-making matters.

A STRUCTURED LEARNING JOURNEY

RIFT is designed to provide a progression from education and practice toward more advanced market participation:

Learn → Demo → Spot → Futures → Smart Money → Automated Execution → Professional Trading

Each stage introduces different concepts, technologies and levels of responsibility.

Rather than focusing solely on individual trades or short-term results, RIFT encourages participants to develop a broader understanding of risk, process, discipline and capital management.

NON-CUSTODIAL INFRASTRUCTURE

RIFT follows a non-custodial approach designed to give users greater control over their own funds and reduce the need to place assets into a centralized company-controlled account.

This reflects a broader movement within digital finance toward greater transparency, user control and blockchain-based infrastructure.

ACCESS FROM ANY DEVICE

RIFT is available through the web as well as its broader platform environment, making it accessible across modern computers, smartphones and other devices.

Its lightweight infrastructure is designed to make participation practical even for users with older devices, helping remove unnecessary technology barriers to accessing modern financial tools.

THE FUTURE OF FINANCIAL PARTICIPATION

Financial markets are changing rapidly.

Trading is becoming increasingly automated. Artificial intelligence is transforming data analysis. Prediction markets are creating new forms of information-based participation. Proprietary trading is expanding access to structured capital allocation models. Blockchain infrastructure is changing how digital assets can be held and transferred.

RIFT brings these developments together within one evolving ecosystem.

RIFT — THE NEXT-GEN AFFILIATE OS

videos.summary_source_text:
What Do the Avalanche Need to Change After the Recent Stretch of Subpar Play? Colorado Avalanche fans question the team’s urgency as a frustrating performance streak raises alarms. With star Gabriel Landeskog bluntly stating “we sucked,” is it time for coach Jared Bednar to shake up the lines or stay patient? Chris Micieli and Zach Pearson break down the Avalanche’s recent lack of execution, missed puck battles, and overreliance on talent, sparking debate about whether small adjustments or bigger changes are needed.

Key topics include Nathan MacKinnon’s role, social media overreactions, and whether shot quantity could reignite the offense. Listeners weigh in on the team’s mindset, the search for “greasy” goals over pretty plays, and the importance of consistent speed. Closing with analysis of Connor Hellebuyck’s trade to the New Jersey Devils and its impact on the Western Conference, the show offers critical insights into what’s next for the Avalanche in a pivotal moment of the NHL season.

videos.title: The Real Cause of Tinnitus (It's Not in Your Ears)
videos.summary_source_text:
The Real Cause of Tinnitus (It's Not in Your Ears) Tinnitus, or ringing in the ears, involves more than just the ears themselves. The brain stem plays an important role in how these phantom sounds are perceived, especially when the inner ear isn’t receiving enough energy to function properly.

Watch the FULL video here: ▶️https://youtu.be/LZNf7O4fqSc 

🌟 Take the 2-minute Health Lever Quiz: https://drbrg.co/47Act5U

Just so you know, my full line of high-quality supplements is available on Amazon — search Dr. Berg Supplements.   

When energy levels in the inner ear drop, the brain stem compensates by increasing its sensitivity to sound. GABA, a neurotransmitter that helps calm nerve activity, normally helps regulate this response.

Vitamin B1 is important for both energy production in the inner ear and GABA function. A deficiency can interfere with these processes and contribute to tinnitus symptoms.

Allithiamine is a form of vitamin B1 originally derived from garlic that can cross the blood-brain barrier and help support energy production and GABA activity in the brainstem.

videos.title: Please STOP Gripping Your Dumbbells Like This!
videos.summary_source_text:
Please STOP Gripping Your Dumbbells Like This! If your wrists hurt when you dumbbell bench press, take a closer look at how you are holding the weights. A small change in your grip may help make this chest exercise more comfortable without completely changing the way you press. In this video, I show you a dumbbell bench press tip that shifts the focus from how much weight you can lift to how your wrists feel while you lift it.

Train Smarter Here - https://athleanx.com
Subscribe to This Channel Here - http://bit.ly/2b0coMW

First, look at your current dumbbell bench press form. Watch the clips in this video and compare them to how you hold your dumbbells, especially at the top of each rep. Are you forcing both ends of the dumbbell to stay perfectly level with the floor? Or do you allow a slight tilt, with your thumb sitting a little higher than your pinky?

The goal here is to find a comfortable, controlled grip that lets you train your chest without your wrists becoming the limiting factor. If every set is interrupted by wrist discomfort, adding more weight is not the answer. Before you worry about progressing your dumbbell bench press, pay attention to where the handle sits in your hand and whether your wrist position changes as you press.

The adjustment shown starts with moving your hand slightly toward the thumb side of the dumbbell handle. Instead of insisting that the dumbbell remain perfectly horizontal, allow the pinky side to sit slightly lower. Watch the demonstration closely. This is a small adjustment in how you hold and balance the weight, not a cue to force your wrist into an exaggerated angle.

Why might this help? The position of the dumbbell in your hand changes how the load is supported at your wrist. A grip that looks symmetrical does not automatically feel comfortable for every person. The video explains the wrist positioning using the radius and ulna, the two bones of the forearm. The practical takeaway is to evaluate whether a subtle change in grip reduces the pinching or pressure you notice during the exercise.

That does not mean every case of wrist pain comes from the same problem, or that one grip adjustment will fix every painful wrist. It means your dumbbell grip is worth checking. Use a light pair of dumbbells to compare the positions shown so that you can focus on control and comfort.

There is another detail to pay attention to: how you squeeze the handle. In the demonstration, the emphasis shifts toward the thumb and index finger. Keep the remaining fingers wrapped securely around the dumbbell for stability. This is not a reason to loosen your hand or let the dumbbell move around during the set.

Think of this as a cue to make your grip more deliberate. Rather than simply grabbing the dumbbells and starting your reps, take a moment to establish the position before you press. Notice where the handle rests, how the dumbbell balances and whether you can maintain that setup throughout the movement. Your grip should feel secure at the bottom, through the press and at the top.

Keep the purpose of the adjustment in mind. We are trying to make the dumbbell bench press more comfortable for your wrists so you can focus on training your chest. You do not need to turn this into a test of how much more weight you can lift. If the lighter dumbbells feel better, practice the setup and make sure the same comfort and control carry over from rep to rep.

Also, do not confuse the slight tilt shown here with allowing the weight to fold your wrist backward. Pay attention to the full demonstration rather than copying only the appearance of the dumbbells at lockout. A useful technique change is one you can control throughout the set, without creating a new uncomfortable position elsewhere.

If you have been searching for how to stop wrist pain during dumbbell bench press, start by watching your grip as closely as you watch your pressing technique. This small detail may be the adjustment that helps you perform the exercise more comfortably. If the change hurts, stop. Persistent or worsening wrist pain deserves an assessment rather than repeated attempts to push through it.

Try the grip adjustment shown in your next chest workout with a light weight and see how your wrists respond. The priority is a secure grip, controlled reps and a chest exercise that feels comfortable.

If you want to apply this tip to a complete workout program, be sure to visit athleanx.com and use the program selector tool to find the program that matches your current goals. By training like an athlete you can see some of your fastest increases in strength and muscle size over the next 90 days.

For more videos on how to fix your aches and pains, especially in the gym, then be sure to subscribe to our channel here on youtube and remember to turn on your notifications so you never miss a new video when it’s published. videos.title: Gemini 5 Is Here: Google’s 10 Trillion Parameter Massive Upgrade!
videos.summary_source_text:
Gemini 5 Is Here: Google’s 10 Trillion Parameter Massive Upgrade! Google's next AI model may already be hiding in plain sight. A leaked internal codename, Carbon, is fueling speculation about Gemini 5, with one Google employee reportedly comparing its coding abilities to Claude Opus 5.5. But there's no benchmark, no official announcement, and no confirmed release date.

Meanwhile, Google's newly released Gemini 4 Argon is already producing some remarkable results: outperforming GPT-6 Astra by roughly 12 points on a long-context benchmark, working autonomously for 11 hours inside a 205,000-line codebase, and powering AI agents that defeated Minecraft's Ender Dragon after 27 hours and 605 deaths.

So what exactly is Google building with Carbon? And could the next Gemini model challenge OpenAI and Anthropic where it matters most?

The story starts with an October 9 Business Insider report revealing three internal Google codenames: Argon, Barium, and Carbon. While speculation has connected Carbon to Gemini 5, the report describes it as a new version of Gemini 4. And Barium-B reportedly became the checkpoint Google selected for Argon.

That distinction changes how we should interpret the leak.

Gemini 4 Argon launched with a roughly one-million-token shared context window, three thinking levels, and introductory API pricing of $2 per million input tokens and $10 per million output tokens. Google also introduced long-running background tasks and continuation-based generation.

But the more interesting story is what Argon can accomplish when connected to external tools.

Argon proposed six performance optimizations across 32 files. Human maintainers rejected four, but two shipped, reducing session-preparation overhead by approximately 40% in long sessions and improving package import performance by roughly 21%.

That's impressive, but it also reveals something important about autonomous AI agents: generating improvements and producing reliable, production-ready code are not the same thing.

Then there's Minecraft.

Four Gemini 4 Argon agents collaborated for 27 hours and 14 minutes, writing 2,783 programs, exchanging 229 messages, and dying 605 times before defeating the Ender Dragon. The experiment demonstrates long-term agent persistence, but it also depended on external memory, coordination systems, and the Mineflayer framework.

The benchmark picture is equally complicated.

On Google's published evaluations, Argon beat GPT-6 Astra on GraphWalks with 84.2 versus 71.8. It also posted strong results on LABBench 2 and the Vals Index.

But coding benchmarks tell a different story.

On Terminal-Bench 4.0, Claude Opus 5.5 scored 66.4 against Argon's 57.4. On FrontierSWE v2, GPT-6 Astra reached 65.5 while Argon managed 55.0.

Google's AI leadership looks very different depending on what you're measuring.

Beyond coding, Google is making ambitious claims about scientific discovery, quantum computing, molecular modeling, robotics, and fusion research.

We examine reported improvements to xTB molecular modeling, a quantum circuit with dramatically reduced spacetime cost, AI-designed enzymes, and a rare-disease genomic analysis.

We also look at Gemini Robotics 2, Boston Dynamics' Spot, simulation-generated robot training, and a reported improvement in real-world robotic task success from 56% to 75%.

But these results come with important qualifications. Some involve publicly inspectable code. Others rely on internal Google evaluations, limited experiments, or research that still requires independent replication.

And that's what makes Carbon so interesting.

If Argon already demonstrates this level of long-context reasoning, autonomous coding, tool orchestration, and scientific assistance, what could Google's next internal checkpoint deliver?

Could Carbon close the gap with Claude Opus 5.5 on coding agents? Could it improve long-running autonomous workflows? And is Google preparing another Gemini 4 model rather than the Gemini 5 release everyone expects?

We separate confirmed releases from leaked information, published benchmarks from company claims, and genuine technical progress from the speculation surrounding Google's next AI model.

Subscribe to BitBiased for detailed coverage of Google Gemini, OpenAI, Anthropic, AI agents, emerging technology, and the competition shaping the next generation of artificial intelligence.

The Truth About Wedge Bounce: Don’t Buy Wedges Until You Watch This Ever wondered: what is wedge bounce, what does bounce on wedges do, and how does it actually impact your chipping? In this video, we break down wedge bounce explained simply—debunking common short game myths and revealing how sole grind and vertical face strike dictate your launch, spin, and scoring.

Most golfers are told that high bounce is for diggers and low bounce is for sweepers, but bounce is completely dynamic. Watch to see how bounce acts as an "insurance policy" through the turf, why sole relief and grind let you open the face cleanly, and how choosing the right sole setup stops thinned chips on hardpan or dead, floating shots out of fluffy grass.

videos.title: Can the TPI Experience Save my Golf Game and Physical Health? | PART 2
videos.summary_source_text:
Can the TPI Experience Save my Golf Game and Physical Health? | PART 2 I’m back at the TPI Performance Centre with Dr Greg Rose, a year on from my last visit, to transform my golf game.

After my first TPI experience, I return to take a deeper look at the dynamics of my swing and understand how my body and movement patterns are influencing the way I play. With Greg’s guidance, I work through a series of stretches and exercises designed to help me move better, then take those learnings onto the range and make some important changes to my swing.

This is all about understanding my game, improving how I move and finding changes that can help me become a better golfer.

The TPI journey continues and this time, we’re making changes.
